title: The same cascade with Panharmonicon cut: does it still kill, and can any version kill a seat at 40?

stack.note: cast for her printed {4}{R}{R} — with The Ur-Dragon's eminence she would cost {3}{R}{R}; the scenario pays full price so the cascade, not the discount, is what is being measured. Identical to stack 002's cast.

scenario.question: This is stack 002's board with PANHARMONICON REMOVED and nothing else changed. (a) Walk the cascade: Miirym's trigger is no longer doubled, so how many nonlegendary Lathliss token copies enter, and what is the total damage from Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest, in how many separately-targeted instances? (b) Is it still lethal to the 32-life seat, which stack 002 kills with 64 damage? (c) Can the damage, optimally assigned, kill a seat at 40 life — either here or in stack 002's four-permanent version, whose own resolution leaves the 40-life seat alive at 8?

extras.context: Stack 002 is checker-passed and resolves the SAME cast with Panharmonicon on the battlefield: two token copies, 64 damage in 12 instances (36 from Terror across six enters-triggers, 28 from Tempest at X = 4,4,5,5,5,5 with optimal ordering), killing the 32-life seat while the 40-life seat survives at 8. Read it before resolving this one; the only difference is the doubler. Note the rules point 002 settled and this scenario inherits: Miirym and Lathliss both read 'another NONTOKEN Dragon you control enters', so the token copies do not re-trigger either of them.
extras.why_this_matters: diagnosis.json's cut_candidates[5] proposes cutting Panharmonicon, and the skeptic established that the cut deletes one of the deck's two checker-passed lethal boards. Nothing on the record says whether that costs 002's LETHALITY or only its MARGIN, and the cut currently rests on a mana argument alone with its decisive evidence named and absent. Part (c) is the deck's central open question: it has two proven kills and neither has been shown to kill a fresh 40-life seat.
extras.scope: One rules domain: trigger counting and damage assignment across one resolving creature spell. No combat, no additional turns. The d20 of Ancient Gold Dragon is stack 001's question and is deliberately not in this board.
